provider.notes: Aliases are the ones registered at gateway/src/plugin/builtin/mod.rs:1729-1730 and matched by the standard factory at gateway/src/core/stt/standard.rs:451-453. An empty model resolves to the default transcriber, for which the gateway omits the transcriber query parameter (gateway/src/core/stt/revai/config.rs:146-151 and 541-553); the vendor treats that as 'machine'. Rev AI needs no segmented path: its live-capable models stream and the gateway already streams to them. Its other transcribers exist only on an asynchronous job API answered in minutes, so they get rows with no transport and a refusal reason, never a file-upload transport. Rev AI has a European deployment (wss://ec1.api.rev.ai/speechtotext/v1/stream/) that the gateway cannot select except through an endpoint override. No transport on this vendor is verified live; the gateway holds no Rev AI key. The gateway's model gate compares the model string exactly, after trimming and without folding case (gateway/src/core/stt/revai/config.rs:540-553), while the map matches ids without regard to case. A session that names 'Machine_V2' therefore lands on the machine_v2 row but the client omits the transcriber parameter and the vendor's default model answers. The resolver must hand the client the row's id, not the customer's spelling. Today's client serves any id its model gate does not recognise, including the deprecated low_cost and fusion, with the account's default streaming model and no warning (gateway/src/core/stt/revai/config.rs:540-553), which is why native_model_handling is substituted.

languages.note: Rev AI's nine streaming languages (vendor streaming request page, confirmed by the fact-check). Mandarin is cmn on the wire; today's client sends any zh tag as cmn (gateway/src/core/stt/revai/config.rs:28-46), so zh is listed too. Every other language exists only on the asynchronous job API; today's client passes it through for Rev AI to refuse.

rates.note: Streaming concurrency limit; Rev AI support can raise it. The audit reads it as account-wide, but the vendor page does not say what it counts against.

context_params.note: A custom vocabulary registered with Rev AI beforehand. The vendor says it cannot be combined with the language parameter, which today's client sends whenever the session language is set (config.rs:465-484); whether language=en with it is rejected is unverified. Not usable with the foreign-language model, which is chosen by the language parameter.

gateway_client.notes: Never exercised against Rev AI: the only end-to-end test runs against an in-repo mock (gateway/tests/mock_endpoint_e2e.rs:9 says the gateway holds no Rev AI key). One long-lived socket per call; each caller chunk is forwarded at once as a binary frame (client.rs:111-116). Vendor 'partial' becomes an interim result and vendor 'final' becomes is_final and is_speech_final (client.rs:327-348). Defects found by reading, none of which stop transcription: partial text is joined with no separator, so interim text reads 'onetooth' (messages.rs:188-190); connect() returns on the HTTP upgrade, not on the vendor 'connected' frame, although the vendor requires waiting for it (client.rs:90-97, 323-326); every vendor final is flagged end of speech although Rev AI finals are commit points, not end-of-utterance markers (client.rs:348); a server Close frame with a standard code such as 1001, 1011, 1012 or 1013 ends the session instead of reconnecting (messages.rs:34-45, 62-64; client.rs:142-157); chunks are not aggregated to the 250 ms the vendor asks for (mod.rs:100 is unused). For this id the gateway omits the transcriber query parameter (config.rs:502-504), which the vendor treats the same as transcriber=machine.
gateway_client.defect: Found by reading, none of which stops transcription: interim text is joined without spaces, every vendor final is flagged end of speech although Rev AI finals are commit points, and a server Close frame with a standard code such as 1001, 1011, 1012 or 1013 ends the session instead of reconnecting (messages.rs:188-190; client.rs:348; messages.rs:62-64 with client.rs:142-157). It also sends audio before the vendor's connected frame and does not aggregate chunks to the 250 ms the vendor asks for (client.rs:90-97; mod.rs:100).

billing.notes: Billing is per stream, not per utterance: Rev AI charges the larger of stream duration and audio duration, rounded up to the second, with a 15 second minimum for each connection, so silence on an open stream is billed. Each connect also places a 10 minute credit hold, and another 5 minutes after every 5 minutes of stream time. Reconnects therefore add minimum charges. There is no Rev AI entry in gateway/src/config/pricing.rs, so no pricing_key is given.

gateway_client.defect: Found by reading, none of which stops transcription: interim text is joined without spaces, every vendor final is flagged end of speech although Rev AI finals are commit points, and a server Close frame with a standard code such as 1001, 1011, 1012 or 1013 ends the session instead of reconnecting (messages.rs:188-190; client.rs:348; messages.rs:62-64 with client.rs:142-157). It also sends audio before the vendor's connected frame and does not aggregate chunks to the 250 ms the vendor asks for (client.rs:90-97; mod.rs:100).

billing.notes: Billing is per stream, not per utterance: Rev AI charges the larger of stream duration and audio duration, rounded up to the second, with a 15 second minimum for each connection, so silence on an open stream is billed. Each connect also places a 10 minute credit hold, and another 5 minutes after every 5 minutes of stream time. Reconnects therefore add minimum charges. There is no Rev AI entry in gateway/src/config/pricing.rs, so no pricing_key is given.

unverified: transports[0].latency (Rev AI publishes no streaming latency; the only figure found was a competitor's claim and is not used)
transports[0].limits.rates[].scope (the vendor states a streaming concurrency limit of 10, adjustable by support; the audit reads it as account-wide but the page does not say)
transports[0].limits.vendor_timeout_ms (whether Rev AI sends WebSocket pings during caller silence is unknown; the gateway treats 60 s without any inbound message as a dead socket, client.rs:44)
transports[0].gateway_client (whether audio sent before the vendor 'connected' frame is dropped or buffered)

whether language=en together with filter_profanity, remove_disfluencies or custom_vocabulary_id is rejected (the vendor text forbids the combination; the gateway sends language whenever the session language is non-empty, config.rs:465-467)
the whole row: an unknown Rev AI id may be an asynchronous-only transcriber, in which case the session is answered by a different model than the one named
provenance.notes: Default for a Rev AI model id the map has never seen. Neither usual rule fits this vendor. File upload cannot be the default, because the only file interface is an asynchronous job answered in minutes. A plain 'every model streams' is not true either, because 'human' and the deprecated 'low_cost' and 'fusion' exist only on the job API. The row keeps today's behaviour, which is the choice that keeps the call working: the existing streaming client serves the session with the account's default streaming model, and the resolver must attach a warning that the capability was assumed. The vendor audit recommends the stricter alternative, refusing unknown ids at setup; the capability-map workstream should decide between the two. No file-upload transport is listed on purpose. Rev AI's only file interface is the asynchronous job API (POST /jobs, then poll or webhook, then GET /jobs/{id}/transcript). The vendor describes its turnaround as '5 minutes or less' for short files, its tutorial says to wait 'approximately 1 minute', and each file is billed a 15 second minimum. The fact-check concluded that Rev AI must never be wrapped in the segmented adapter. Opening one short socket per utterance and sending EOS to force a final was also rejected: each connection bills 15 seconds, places a 10 minute credit hold and counts against the limit of 10 concurrent streams. The provider's native_model_handling (substituted) is what makes the resolver attach that warning.
